claim_verdicts.evidence: Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). RFC 9110 §3.3 (line 768): "HTTP is defined as a stateless protocol, meaning that each request message's semantics can be understood in isolation, and that the relationship between connections and messages on them has no impact on the interpretation of those messages."

Carried from prior review (claim unchanged). RFC 9110 §3.3 (line 778): "a server MUST NOT assume that two requests on the same connection are from the same user agent unless the connection is secured and specific to that agent." RFC 9112 §9.3: persistent connections carry several requests. Current §4 text "One TCP connection can carry several requests one after another, but it only moves bytes" matches. Live 2026-09-27 06:44: one curl -v with two /admin URLs prints "Reusing existing http: connection with host localhost".
claim_verdicts.source: refs/rfc/rfc9112.txt; refs/rfc/rfc9110.txt; live curl -v in donhang-lab

claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 6265 s3 L299-302: "To store state, the origin server includes a Set-Cookie header in an HTTP response. In subsequent requests, the user agent returns a Cookie request header to the origin server. The Cookie header contains cookies the user agent received in previous Set-Cookie headers." Lab capture steps 2 and 4 agree. Key http_cookies fits.

RFC 6265 s4.1.1 L456: set-cookie-string = cookie-pair *( ";" SP cookie-av ) - one pair per Set-Cookie; s3 L315: "Origin servers SHOULD NOT fold multiple Set-Cookie header fields into a single header field." s4.2.1 L701: cookie-string = cookie-pair *( ";" SP cookie-pair ) - several pairs on one Cookie line.

RFC 6265 s5.4: cookie-list holds cookies whose host-only domain is identical to (or domain-matches) the request-host, "The request-uri's path path-matches the cookie's path", and if secure-only-flag "the request-uri's scheme must denote a \"secure\" protocol (as defined by the user agent)"; L1363: "A user agent MAY omit the Cookie header in its entirety." Lab: -b adds only the header, /admin then 200.

RFC 6265 s4.1.2.4 L642-644: "The user agent will include the cookie in an HTTP request only if the path portion of the request-uri matches (or is a subdirectory of) the cookie's Path attribute" - every path is under "/".

RFC 6265 s4.1.2.6 L681-684: the HttpOnly attribute "instructs the user agent to omit the cookie when providing access to cookies via \"non-HTTP\" APIs (such as a web browser API that exposes cookies to scripts)."

RFC 6265 s4.1.2.5 L652-658: "The Secure attribute limits the scope of the cookie to \"secure\" channels (where \"secure\" is defined by the user agent)... only if the request is transmitted over a secure channel (typically HTTP over ... TLS)". s8.3 L1665-1666: "Unless sent over a secure channel (such as TLS), the information in the Cookie and Set-Cookie headers is transmitted in the clear." L686: HttpOnly "is independent of the Secure attribute".
